verdict.reasoning: Patient states she "can't quite move my left arm... it's numb" and also feels "some like tingling in my fingertips," confirming numbness and tingling in the left arm and fingers.
Patient says symptoms have been present "for at least two weeks and it's kind of gotten worse" referring to the left arm tingling and subsequent numbness.
Patient specifies tingling/numbness in "my second, third and fourth finger" and clarifies it is on "the front side" (palm side).
Patient reports it is "harder to get the notes" when playing piano and agrees to "mild weakness" in the left arm, saying "it's not hurting. It's like numb. I can't feel it."
When asked about neck pain, patient responds, "No, not. No neck pain."
Patient links onset to starting boxing: "I've started taking this boxing class... it's probably been, I'd say for at least two weeks" and numbness/tingling developed and worsened after that.

Patient describes "a really bad cold... probably good, like, two weeks" and separately "all of a sudden just couldn't see... from my left eye" with loss of field of vision that "just lasted maybe for, I don't know, 20, 20 minutes."
Patient says, "I do take ibuprofen... I've just kind of taken ibuprofen" for pain.
Patient states, "vitamin D, I take."
Patient reports, "sometimes I take melatonin to help me sleep," which indicates occasional use.
Patient notes her GP wants her to take iron but, "they are this like huge pill, so I, most of the time I just forget," indicating non-compliance.
Patient says, "my dad has... I think it's hypothyroidism" and "he's got some autoimmune stuff going on."
Patient reports her mother has "diabetes, type 2," "hypertension," and "high cholesterol," which corresponds to dyslipidemia.
Transcript mentions a specific heavy drinking event ("we were like out partying") but does not state her usual or occasional alcohol use pattern.

Patient describes being "out, you know, drinking with friends" and "uncharacteristically drunk" and "we kind of went crazy and we were like out partying until, you know, late hours," supporting a recent heavy drinking episode.
The transcript contains only history and assessment; there are no documented physical exam findings, so stating none are documented is accurate.
The discussion centers on "numbness in the left arm" and "tingling" in the fingers; these are the main problems assessed.

Symptoms began after starting boxing class, and the doctor states, "I'm just wondering whether there's something a bit more than just the box in here" and considers neurologic causes such as MS, indicating possible neurologic origin beyond boxing.
Doctor explicitly revisits the episode: "You mentioned for a while you couldn't see... peripheral vision from your left eye," showing transient left eye vision loss is part of the assessment.

Doctor states, "Sometimes, you know, you do get things like ms, multiple sclerosis. So people with multiple sclerosis can have visual problems like what you've experienced," directly linking MS as a possible cause of her transient visual symptoms.
Patient mentions a prior viral-like illness, but the doctor does not state that the viral illness is a contributing factor to current neurologic symptoms.
Doctor says, "I'm going to do an urgent, very urgent neurology referral," clearly outlining this plan.
Doctor notes neurology referral "might entail is the brain scan and things like that" in the context of evaluating for MS, implying brain imaging is being considered.

Doctor advises monitoring: "if the weakness progresses to your legs or there's any kind of headaches, vomiting, fits, and your visual symptoms are getting worse and not getting better, then that would be" an urgent situation, indicating a plan to watch for progression of these symptoms.
